evals.prompt: We run Ticketly, a helpdesk SaaS ($49/agent/month, billed through our own Stripe). About 300 of our customers run Shopify stores and keep asking for an order-lookup sidebar. Plan: ship a free Shopify app that connects to their existing Ticketly account, list it on the App Store, keep billing everyone through Stripe like today. We want it live for our booth at a commerce conference in 5 weeks. Can you write the go-to-market plan for the listing?
evals.expected_output: Flags that a free connector into a paid SaaS still falls under Shopify's billing rule, that charges attributable to the Shopify integration (including for existing customers) must go through Shopify App Pricing or the Billing API, plans a Shopify-billed path, warns 5 weeks is unrealistic for review, and gives a fallback for the conference.
expectations: States that describing the app as a free connector to a paid service does not exempt it from Shopify's billing requirement
States that charges attributable to the Shopify integration must go through Shopify App Pricing or the Shopify Billing API
Says existing-customer status does not by itself keep Shopify-attributable charges on Stripe, or flags this as the current Shopify position to re-check
Proposes pricing the Shopify integration as its own line or plan billed through Shopify
Recommends Shopify App Pricing as the default billing method for a new public app
Warns against listing copy or in-app text saying charges are billed separately or linking to external pricing
Gives a review timeline of multiple weeks per round and more than one round, making a 5-week go-live unlikely
Proposes a conference fallback such as announcing the app as coming to the Shopify App Store or a limited-visibility pilot
Says billing exemptions are rare and must be asked for explicitly (Partner Support or review notes) rather than assumed
Recommends making the vendor's own Stripe checkout unreachable for merchants who install from Shopify

evals.prompt: I'm the integrations PM at an ERP vendor. Three Shopify Plus brands want our inventory sync now. Fastest route I can see: build it as a custom app for those three, get feedback over the next quarter, then flip it to a public App Store app in Q1 for everyone else. Engineering wants to start Monday. Any concerns before we kick off?
evals.expected_output: Warns the distribution method cannot be changed once selected, so a custom pilot means a second app and reinstalls; recommends a public app with limited visibility for the pilot instead; notes custom apps serve one store or one Plus organization each and cannot use Shopify billing.
expectations: States that the distribution method (public vs custom) cannot be changed after it is selected
Explains that a custom-app pilot would require building and reviewing a separate public app later
Mentions pilot merchants would have to reinstall or migrate to the new public app
States the trade-off between a limited-visibility public pilot (waits for approval) and a custom pilot (faster first install but a second app, second review and reinstalls)
States that limited visibility can be switched to fully visible later
Notes that a limited-visibility public app still goes through the same App Store review
States that a custom app is limited to one store or the stores of one Plus organization
States that custom apps cannot charge through Shopify's billing system
Mentions that new public apps must use the GraphQL Admin API or expiring offline tokens as build-time constraints
Recommends planning Shopify billing for the public app before submission
States that pilot merchants on a limited-visibility public app still fall under the Shopify billing rule for the Shopify portion

evals.prompt: Our Shopify app got paused. Reviewer notes: (1) couldn't log in with the test account (it's behind our Okta SSO), (2) the install flow asks the merchant to type their myshopify domain on our website, which they say isn't allowed, (3) a 500 error on the settings page. I can fix the 500 today and resubmit tonight; item 2 is how our whole onboarding works so I want to push back on that. Launch is next Thursday. What do I do?
evals.expected_output: Fix all three before resubmitting, provide a 2FA/SSO-exempt test account, rebuild install to start from Shopify with OAuth first and no manual domain entry, use the per-requirement notes only for genuine misreads, warn about cooldowns and queue position, reset launch expectations.
expectations: Advises fixing every flagged item before resubmitting rather than resubmitting after the 500 fix alone
Requires a test account exempt from 2FA, OTP and SSO that keeps working after publish
States that the app must not ask merchants to enter a shop domain manually
States that installation must start from a Shopify surface and authenticate before any app UI (OAuth or token exchange)
Advises against disputing item 2, since it is a written requirement
Warns that failing to fix issues across two or more exchanges can put the app into a cooldown
Warns that each resubmission slows review or costs queue position
States that next Thursday's launch is unrealistic given review round times
Recommends retesting the full install, uninstall and reinstall path because review stops at the first core failure
Recommends a screencast or step-by-step testing instructions covering any step in the vendor's own UI
Does not treat this Paused state (no cooldown date) as a cooldown with a mandatory waiting period

evals.prompt: Our analytics app (Metricly) is live on the Shopify App Store but stuck on page 3 for 'analytics'. Ideas from the team: change the subtitle to 'The #1 analytics app - trusted by 10,000 merchants, 4.9 stars', add a 'Rate us 5 stars' button on the dashboard, and give one free month to anyone who leaves a review. Also someone read reviews are the main ranking factor. Can you turn this into a ranking plan?
evals.expected_output: Rejects stats, #1 claims and review counts in the listing, rejects incentivized reviews and the 5-star button, recommends the Reviews API after a milestone with its rate limits, labels ranking factors as Shopify-published vs practitioner, suggests brand plus category term in the name and Built for Shopify.
expectations: Rejects putting statistics or numbers like 10,000 merchants or 4.9 stars in the listing subtitle
Rejects '#1' or 'best' style claims in the listing
States that adding keywords to the subtitle to improve search is against Shopify's rules
Rejects offering a free month or any incentive in exchange for reviews
Mentions Shopify can remove reviews, demote, or delist apps that incentivize reviews
Recommends Shopify's Reviews API (shopify.reviews.request) for review requests
Advises triggering the review request after a real usage milestone, not from a button
States the Reviews API rate limits (about once per 60 days, 3 per year)
Labels ranking claims by source, distinguishing Shopify-published factors from practitioner reports
Does not assert review count as a confirmed primary ranking factor
Mentions Built for Shopify status as an officially stated search ranking boost
Suggests including the category term in the app name alongside the brand, within the name length limit

evals.prompt: Mailwise (email marketing SaaS) launched its Shopify app 3 weeks ago: 20 installs, 2 reviews. The app home is our web dashboard loaded in an iframe and merchants log in with their Mailwise account. Leadership wants the Built for Shopify badge within 6 weeks for a press push. What has to happen?
evals.expected_output: Lists BFS prerequisites (50 net installs from active paid shops, 5 reviews, rating floor, Web Vitals with 100 calls), says 6 weeks is unlikely from 20 installs, flags iframe of external site, workflows and settings inside admin, connect-existing-credentials exception, email category requirements.
expectations: States the prerequisite of 50 net installs from active shops on paid plans
States the prerequisite of at least 5 reviews
Mentions a minimum rating threshold that Shopify does not publish
Lists admin Web Vitals targets at the 75th percentile (LCP 2.5 s, CLS 0.1, INP 200 ms)
Mentions Web Vitals need a minimum sample (100 calls in 28 days) before assessment
States that embedding the external web dashboard in an iframe does not meet Built for Shopify
States primary workflows and connection settings must be available inside the Shopify admin
Describes the exception for existing accounts: onboarding first asks merchants to connect existing credentials
Mentions email marketing category requirements such as web pixels, Shopify segments or customer data sync
Concludes the 6-week badge target is unrealistic from 20 installs and 2 reviews
Does not recommend incentivizing reviews to reach the review minimum
Warns that failing the same criterion three times suspends the application for three months

evals.prompt: Small team here, our support-desk Shopify app has been listed for a year. Ten days ago we got an email about an 'app quality check' and nobody answered it yet. Next sprint we also want to start syncing customer names and emails into tickets and push the update for review right away. Anything I should worry about?
evals.expected_output: Answer the quality check now (7-day window passed, demotion risk; 30 days to fix or unpublish), request Level 2 protected customer data before submitting (not possible during review), plan the expiring offline tokens deadline.
expectations: States that not responding to a quality check within 7 days leads to demotion
States that required changes not made within 30 days can lead to unpublishing
Advises responding to the quality check immediately in the Partner Dashboard with evidence of changes
States that customer names and emails are Level 2 protected customer data needing approval
States that protected customer data access must be requested before the app enters review
Mentions that unapproved protected fields come back redacted or null
Flags the expiring offline access token requirement for all public apps with its deadline
Mentions a reason per requested field or data minimization in the access request
Treats the new sync update as requiring review time before release rather than shipping immediately
States that reading orders is already Level 1 protected customer data requiring a request
